$comment: Model tiers are the portable way anycrew says how much model an agent needs. Each tool maps a tier to its own model name here. Override per project in .anycrew/config.json under "models". Keep aliases (not dated IDs) wherever the tool offers them so the mapping ages well.

fast.purpose: Read, search, summarise, format, update status docs, mechanical edits. High volume, low stakes.

balanced.purpose: Implement a task, write tests, routine review, research with sources, infra and deploy work.

strong.purpose: Decisions and judgement: brainstorm, product scope, architecture, specs, security, final review, hard debugging, LLM feature design.

claude.$comment: Claude Code subagent frontmatter: `model:` accepts haiku | sonnet | opus | fable | inherit | full ID; `effort:` accepts low | medium | high | xhigh | max.

antigravity.$comment: Antigravity subagents (.agents/agents/*.md) accept `model: inherit | flash | pro` (tiers, not IDs). `flash_lite` exists only for run_workflow scripts, so fast and balanced both map to flash.

gemini.$comment: Gemini CLI model names. Adjust to the models your account can use.

codex.$comment: Codex custom agents (.codex/agents/*.toml) take `model` and `model_reasoning_effort` (low | medium | high | xhigh | max). `model` null keeps the user's default model and varies only the effort.

cursor.$comment: Cursor subagents accept `model: inherit` or a model ID such as composer-2 or claude-opus-5[effort=high]. inherit keeps the chat's model; set IDs here to enforce tiers.

opencode.$comment: OpenCode agents take `model: provider/model-id`. Defaults assume the Anthropic provider; change to your provider.

copilot.$comment: GitHub Copilot custom agents accept `model:` as a string or a preference-ordered array; empty means inherit the chat's model.
